Verne (A33)

Survey region: Empire of Anbennar (EoA).

One-sentence positioning: Bring the lost wyvern riders back into the sky, then carry Vernmen adventurism from the imperial frontier across Halann.

Story: very high｜Mission-tree length: long (48 direct missions)｜Mission-tree update: the 2025 The Final Empire rework is released; the local mission file was modified on 2026-07-09 and supports v1.37.5.0｜Distinctiveness: very high｜Grind: medium-high｜Early pressure: medium-high｜Expansion capacity: high

Identity and History

Verne (A33) is a Vernman duchy within the Empire of Anbennar in 1444, with its capital in the Luna basin. It begins in the Regent Court, ruled by the reformist Alvar IV síl Verne; Pearlsedge is its historic rival, while Eborthíl is a historic ally. Verne's coast and its proximity to the Khenak Mountains together give rise to its seafaring and wyvern-rider traditions.

The offline English Wiki traces the old Kingdom of Verne to the kingdom founded in 479 by Armoc I, who had tamed a wyvern famous for its riders. Verne later fell under Damerian hegemony, was reorganised as a duchy in 1207 and seceded from Dameria in 1257. It supported the síl Muna faction in the Lilac Wars and fought alongside the Eborthíli fleet. The kingdom's glory is now only a memory: wyvern riding has been lost, and the mountain wyverns are threatened by arcanists and poachers. Duke Alvar wants to restore the tradition, but Verne cannot begin in 1444 with a mature aerial cavalry force. The offline Wiki also contains a later chronology about a revival in 1504; that is setting history, not an inevitable in-game year.

National Story and Campaign Arc

The reworked mission tree begins by asking what the Vernmen are supposed to be: proud of moustaches, bravery, adventure and a somewhat reckless heroism, yet forced to face old nobles, post-war refugees, trade competition and backward social structures. Alvar's reforms are not merely about giving the knights wings; they must also make the duchy wealthy, maritime, educated and willing to leave its old borders.

The story then opens in three directions at once. Into the mountains, it seeks wyvern eggs and rebuilds nests, taming methods and wyvern riders. Along the coast, it reaches Aelantir, Sarhal and still farther lands through adventurer ports, expeditions and an exhibition, collecting stories and relics. In the Old World, it contests Pearlsedge, Busilar and other rivals while trying to bring Corinite ideas of justice into imperial politics. The late missions even combine wyverns, artifice and the navy. These are routes the player can pursue, not an imperial realm that already exists in 1444.

Core Mechanics

  1. Rebuilding the wyvern riders: Find eggs, establish nests and complete the taming work before the missions unlock the Wyvern Mythic Cavalry. Early preparation involves mage support; lacking the right magical resources can create long-term debt. Wyvern leaders, nest expansion and later sea platforms gradually turn “riding wyverns” into a national institution.
  2. Adventure decisions and adventurer ports: Once unlocked, decisions can dispatch expeditions to specified locations, complete cross-regional adventures and return unique results. Adventurer ports, colonial outposts and fleets determine whether the story can reach the far side of the sea; this is not a snowball based only on colonist numbers.
  3. The Verne exhibition: Treasures and discoveries from expeditions enter an exhibition system that gradually expands Verne's cultural centre. Exhibits justify the next story beat and link conquest, scholarship and conspicuous national projects.
  4. Religion and imperial politics: The country begins in the Regent Court; a Corinite turn, imperial elections and religious wars open later routes. Verne wants to reform the Empire in the name of heroism, but also uses war and conversion to expand its influence, so later faith cannot be projected back onto 1444.
  5. Overseas colonisation and artifice: The missions guide the establishment of New World bases and gradually combine wyvern riders, the navy and artifice research. Some colonies may be renamed “New Verne”, but that is a subject-name change, not a Tag change for A33.

Phased Play

In the early game, use Alvar's abilities to improve the economy, secure the Luna and the bay, contest Pearlsedge and watch the costs of mountain and magical development. The new mission tree places wyverns relatively late, so the old impression of powerful cavalry from day one is a bad basis for planning wars. Players commonly mention tight early finances; one detailed guide also used submods and a development branch, so its exact amounts should not be copied as current rules.

In the middle game, organise the navy, colonies and expeditions, linking the adventurer ports to Aelantir and the southern routes while preserving your political position in the Old World so that the wyvern nests can be expanded. The late-game challenge is not only combat strength: wyvern breeding, the exhibition, a Corinite Empire and overseas ventures all compete for money, armies, diplomatic attention and time. Players who want one or two decisive wars may find the objectives too dispersed.

Formable Country and Endgame

The Verne route keeps A33 as its identity; there is no need to split the “Kingdom of Verne” missions or the colonial subject “New Verne” into new country entries. The missions allow Verne to seek a higher position within the imperial system, contest maritime power to the south and turn wyvern culture into a transcontinental identity. This is a future in which an old duchy becomes a world power, not a fixed historical outcome.

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 86/100｜Autocracy 55/100｜Magic↔Artifice 55/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 77/100)｜Pluralism 65/100.

The v2.1 value score is Good (79/100), with a stable trajectory. Permanent abolition of slavery, greater tolerance for remnants and anti-oppression themes are clear positive evidence; colonisation, war and religious transformation mainly reduce restraint and do not automatically pull the country back to neutral.

Recommended for players who enjoy wyvern cavalry, adventure events, maritime colonisation and imperial politics woven together. The reworked Verne is not easy if you want wyverns immediately or dislike managing expensive colonial, magical and religious objectives in parallel.

Community Experience and Evidence Boundary

The official 2025 dev diary and release announcements confirm the Verne mission-tree rework and its adventure and wyvern themes. Two newer player posts consider it longer and more expensive than the old tree, with greater emphasis on Pearlsedge, Busilar and overseas routes; the long guide used several submods and a development branch, so it is experience evidence only. Current missions, mechanics and names follow the local Mod and localisation; the offline Wiki supplies history only. Cross-year projections from the Halann historical map are not written as inevitable history.

For complete sources, paths and conflicts, see the evidence record.

National ideas (reference appendix)

Native English national-idea names and descriptions are reproduced below with the inherited effect displays. Traditions apply when this set is adopted; its seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Alternative sets and successor ideas do not automatically stack. Descriptions may recount history or depict future ideals, not events already completed in 1444. Native English wording is reused rather than back-translating embellished Chinese localisation. Inherited display-unit assumptions remain unverified; this translation does not correct source data.

Verne (A33) — Vernman Ideas

Traditions: Vernman Traditions

Effects: Leader land shock: +1; Production efficiency: +15%.

Idea 1: Legacy of the Wyvern Riders

As the Dragonwake unfolded, the Vernid people united behind Armoc Vernid, the first wyvern-rider and the first to bear the title of Wyvern-King. After its creation, the nascent kingdom rose high, even rivalling the warlords of Wex and the fallen moon of the Damerians. Armoc I Vernid built a great legacy, one of crimson wings casting their shadow along the Luna.

Yet, all that rise must fall, and much like the realms that Verne had eclipsed, it too was defeated and was brought under the Damerian hegemony. Verne has now lost its greatness, the wyvern-riders no longer scour the skies. The crimson wings have retreated to the mountains, on the brink of extinction at the hand of cruel arcanists and greedy poachers. Their protection ensured by teams of state-hired Vernmen adventurers, who hunt down would-be poachers all across the western Khenak range. But this does not mean wyvern-riding shall remain a relic of the past as it might yet be restored by the great men that lead Verne.

“Our legacy is old but not forgotten. Verne, its people and its Duke still dream of this past glory. But we will dream no longer. May all heed my words, wyverns will fly under our banners once more, and Verne shall rise !” - Alvar IV síl Verne - 1461

Effects: Monarch military skill: +1; Army tradition from battles: +0.5.

Idea 2: Pearlescent Rivals

Verne and Pearlsedge are the bitterest of rivals, their naval ambitions are at odds as both nations desire to assert their dominance on the entrance to the Dameshead. This disagreement has evolved into a permanent trade war, where ships often trade hands in less than amicable manner. As such our traders and sailors are quite experienced in “offensive exchange” of goods (and ammunition).

During this commercial conflict the Pearlsedger sometimes attacked and captured Vernmen trade ships to confiscate their goods. In 1425, the daring captain Andrel of Napesbay devised a tactic to deceive the corsairs and conduct an important trade mission successfully. He filled the trade ship with worthless half-rotten lobsters, while the escort ship contained the valuable cargo. When the Pearlsedger corsairs approached, the dummy trade ship surrendered while the light and fast escort seemingly fled and carried out its mission successfully. Even though this act was done without warning his superiors or the crown, the great success he achieved made him rise to the rank of admiral in charge of Verne’s fleets.

The sailors present on that mission spread the story across our ports and quickly the moniker “dull lobster” was attributed to the Pearlsedgers, an act of spite that is still mentioned to this day.

Effects: Embargo efficiency: +25%; Chance to Capture Enemy Ships: +10%.

Idea 3: The Heartspier Scale

As Aelantir was rediscovered and the call of adventure sounded across Cannor, the greatest adventurers came to a strange land, full of powerful beasts and ancient secrets. And among the greatest of these men were the Vernmen!

Soon, adventurer towns populated the continent, with many Vernmen cropping up across the new continent, from north to south. These were rallying points for those that sought a new life, whether that be to delve deep in dangerous precursor ruins, challenge the river lords of the Ynn and even facing the darkness deep in the heart of the Effe’lai.

And keeping with Vernmen tradition, colonial backing from the duchy was granted not by favour or proposals, but by great feats themselves. As established by Duke Alvar VI in 1553, such as:

A great mustachio - State sponsored equipment Discovery of a precursor ruin - Funds and expedition rights for said ruin Sinking a pirate ship - Command of a ship in the navy Conquest of a rival settlement - Governorship of said settlement Killing a great beast of the Effe’lai - Generalship and Naming of a settlement in one’s name

“Such is the way of the Vernmen, putting forth Great Men (and Great Mustachios) for all to witness.” - Erning of Heartspier on the origin of the Great Men Great Mustachios theory.

Effects: Settler growth: +2500%; Envoy travel time: -25%.

Idea 4: The Red-Brass guns

Vernmen bronze, erroneously called Red-Brass by many, is a special grade of bronze solely produced in Verne since ancient times. Its grade is achieved by using very low lead content tin that is only found in the western Khenak. This makes Vernmen bronze extremely strong and highly adapted for many uses in the military industry. Its uses and value increased even further when the age of gunpowder came about as it was the perfect metal for cannons. In Verne, this metal is used to produce a famous line of cannons, coloured deep red on the exterior through a specific process and giving them the moniker “Red-Brass guns”. This eventually led to the creation of the mercantile company Vernmen Bronze & Artillery by the síl na Bronzewing family, which had a complete monopoly on the export of Red-Brass in the Empire.

Rumours mention that the “Red-Brass guns” were initially designed to be mounted onto wyverns, enabling terrifying hit and run tactics. But these efforts, if true, never yielded results. Instead, the modern wyvern-riders use “wyvern-roar” ordinance, dropping them from the sky to spread terror in the enemy ranks before performing devastating diving attacks in the enemy ranks. This tactic is similar to the Eborthili naval doctrine of spreading terror through the continuous roar of cannons.

Effects: Artillery fire: +25%; Heavy ship cost: -10%.

Idea 5: The Birthplace of the Regatta

In 1523 the first official Wyvern’s Sting Regatta was held, a boat race organised by the mayors of the many ports on the shores of the Wyvern’s Gulf. Since then, eager youngsters and hardy sailors alike take part in the yearly race, departing from Watchman’s Point and arriving in Stingport. The perilous course used for the event, going around the gulf and its many rocky islets, was initially used as a challenge for sailors to settle their disputes in friendly manners as navigating this path requires a modicum of skill.

The event caught the attention of sailors abroad, and in 1641 the first ever team regatta was organised, with teams hailing from Eborthil and Anbenncóst. In the following decade new regattas were established on new courses such as touring the Isle of Tef or the Damesear, and even, for the more adventurous, travelling from Strongport to Ekha.

With the discovery of a southern seaway passing by Kheionai, Ardimya and southern Insyaa, a new route is being planned. A grand course touring the globe for what many call “The Grand Regatta”.

Effects: Sailor Modifier: +20%; Prestige: +0.5.

Idea 6: The First Corinite Emperors

Anbennar has long been the battleground of Cannorian faith, and in 1648 the First Corinite War was brought to an end with the Peace of Esmaria, allowing any Cannorian to become emperor, whether they be Adeanic, Corinite or even the new Ravelian faith. And so in 1648, in the wake of peace, Emperor Alvar I síl Verne ascended the throne as the first Corinite Emperor. In his speech he retraced the faith's origins in Verne, from the influence of the Brave Brothers to Ardor II's declaration for Corinism in 1519, one of the few princes who converted before the Crimson Deluge. Upon his ascension Alvar I declared: "The Corinite War has ended!"

He was wrong.

For the next half century the imperial seat switched hands between the Vernmen and their eternal rivals, the Pearlsedgers. Whilst for most of that period the empire traded peace for intrigue and colonial skirmishes, it entrenched the Corinite faith in Anbennar proper, and showed the people will not stand for tyranny and decadence any longer. The bitter rivalry eventually sparked war once more, for there can be no peace whilst evil remained, and in 1675 the Second Corinite War saw the near-collapse of the House of Verne, that was, until they invited a foreign Corinite King to come home at least: Camir Silmuna.

Effects: Army morale: +15%; Yearly Corinite Paragonhood decay: raw value 0.1 (unit unverified).

Idea 7: The Homeland of Great Adventurers

Ours brothers brave to Escann went And in Athfork cold in sodden tent The captain cried in grave lament She'd hacked down every foe

Here is a Vernman’s son, Adventure is where he belongs, Battles fierce, swiftly won, Wherever he shall go.

Sailors sure to Valorpoint And thieves then fear their flags ahoist And lead the Concords’ fleet conjoint To blast sea monsters low.

Here is a Vernman’s son, Adventure is where he belongs, Battles fierce, swiftly won, Wherever he shall go

To Drakesguard proud our sons embarked To look for treasure in the dark In Amadia they found loves’ spark And treasures they sure found, oh!

Here is a Vernman’s son, Adventure is where he belongs, Maidens’ fair are deftly won, Wherever he shall go

Many greats are Vernmen sons Adventure’s home in Verne belongs, Mustachios and shoulders strong, Our pay will not be low!

Vernmen's Son Unknown Author, Compiled by Edward Alen-Gerwicksson
